mcqs.q: Patient informatics is also known as:
mcqs.explain: Patient informatics (consumer informatics) is a new aspect of medical informatics reflecting the empowered healthcare consumer.

mcqs.q: Which is one of the four topics of patient informatics?
mcqs.explain: The four topics are internet education, web portals, personal health records, and patient–physician communication.

mcqs.q: Which group is MOST likely to seek health information online?
opts: Women, under 65, college graduates with broadband access
mcqs.explain: Those most likely to seek health information online are women, aged under 65, college graduates, with more online experience and broadband access.

mcqs.q: A reason for the increased use of the Internet in healthcare is that patients:
opts: Expect tech-savvy physicians and would switch if they are not
mcqs.explain: Patients expect their physicians to be tech-savvy and would consider switching if they are not; care is also more patient-centered and organisations use IT for marketing.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of an online patient-education website?
mcqs.explain: Examples include WebMD, Revolution Health, MedlinePlus, Healthfinder and FamilyDoctor.

mcqs.q: MedlinePlus offers content in approximately how many languages?
mcqs.explain: MedlinePlus has 700+ health topics, 165 tutorials, surgical videos and content available in 40 languages.

mcqs.q: A patient web portal is best described as:
opts: A web-based program patients access for health-related services
mcqs.explain: Web portals are web-based programs patients access for health-related services; they can be standalone or integrated with an EHR.

mcqs.q: A patient web portal can be:
opts: Standalone or integrated with an electronic health record
mcqs.explain: A web portal can be a standalone program or it can be integrated with an electronic health record.

mcqs.q: A personal health record (PHR) is defined as:
opts: An electronic, universally available, lifelong resource of health information for making health decisions
mcqs.explain: A PHR is an electronic, universally available, lifelong resource of health information needed by individuals to make health decisions.

mcqs.q: Which is an IDEAL feature of a PHR?
mcqs.explain: Ideal PHR features: portable, interoperable, auto-populated, patient-controlled, longitudinal, private/secure, and fitting the clinician's workflow.

mcqs.q: A PHR being 'portable' means it:
opts: Follows the patient even when job, insurer or clinician changes
Can only be carried by the doctor
mcqs.explain: Portable means the information follows you even when there is a job, insurer or clinician change.

mcqs.q: A 'tethered' PHR is one that is:
opts: Connected to one platform and not interoperable
mcqs.explain: A tethered PHR is connected to one platform and is not interoperable; untethered PHRs are not tied to one platform and have more interoperability.

mcqs.q: Google Health and Microsoft HealthVault are examples of:
mcqs.explain: Untethered PHRs (web-based or mobile) include examples like Google Health and Microsoft HealthVault.

mcqs.q: Which is one of the four forms of patient–physician communication?
opts: Secure email, e-visits, telephonic visits and audio-video televisits
mcqs.explain: The four forms are secure email, electronic visits, telephonic visits and audio-video televisits.

mcqs.q: Regarding secure email, the literature suggests:
opts: Patients want it, but most physicians are less enthusiastic
Physicians love it but patients refuse
mcqs.explain: Studies suggest patients want to communicate by email, but that enthusiasm is not shared by most physicians.

mcqs.q: Why do physicians cite reluctance to use email with patients?
opts: Liability, poor compensation, privacy issues and untrained staff
mcqs.explain: Physicians cite liability, poor compensation, privacy issues, untrained staff, and a feeling that face-to-face visits are better.

mcqs.q: A benefit of email communication is that it is:
opts: Asynchronous — physicians answer at their convenience, avoiding 'phone tag'
mcqs.explain: Email is asynchronous (answer at convenience, avoiding phone tag), has lower overhead, is self-documenting, saves work time and is faster, with high satisfaction.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of email messaging with patients is:
opts: Inability to examine the patient and potential communication errors
mcqs.explain: Disadvantages include indigent patients using it less, inability to examine the patient, communication errors, slow responses, security issues and being overwhelmed.

mcqs.q: Electronic visits (e-visits) are an example of:
mcqs.explain: E-visits (virtual visits) are an example of telehealth or telemedicine, where medical care is delivered remotely.

mcqs.q: E-visits specifically require:
mcqs.explain: E-visits require secure messaging (not routine e-mail), giving better security/privacy and the ability to involve a third party in billing.

mcqs.q: A telephonic visit service (e.g. TelaDoc) typically will NOT:
mcqs.explain: TelaDoc guarantees a callback (e.g. within 3 hours) and will prescribe and handle refills, but will not prescribe narcotics or order labs.

mcqs.q: American Well is an example of which communication form?
mcqs.explain: American Well lets patients interact with clinicians using web-based videoconferencing, secure chat and telephonic communication — an audio-video televisit.

saqs.q: Define patient informatics and list its four topics.
saqs.a: Patient (consumer) informatics is a new aspect of medical informatics reflecting the empowered healthcare consumer. Topics: internet for patient education, web portals, personal health records, and patient–physician communication.

saqs.q: Give reasons for the increased use of the Internet in healthcare.
saqs.a: Care is more patient-centered; quality education sites abound; patients want the best care at lowest cost; they expect tech-savvy physicians (and would switch); organisations use IT as a marketing tool; and searching is fast and easy.

saqs.q: List the ideal features of a PHR.
saqs.a: Portable, interoperable, auto-populated, patient-controlled, longitudinal, private & secure, and fitting the clinician's workflow.
Tethered = connected to one platform and not interoperable. Untethered = not tied to one platform, with more interoperability (web-based or mobile; e.g. Google Health, Microsoft HealthVault).

saqs.q: State the benefits and disadvantages of patient-physician email.
saqs.a: Benefits: asynchronous (answer at convenience, avoids phone-tag), low overhead, self-documenting, saves work time, faster, high satisfaction. Disadvantages: indigent patients use it less, no physical exam, communication errors, slow replies, security, and being overwhelmed.

saqs.q: Name the four forms of patient-physician communication and an example of a televisit service.
saqs.a: Secure email, electronic visits, telephonic visits, audio-video televisits. Telephonic example: TelaDoc; audio-video example: American Well.
